sky.name: Sky
sky.description: The first four houses are occupied by major celestial figures: Tinia, the supreme god linked to Zeus and Jupiter; Cilens, a deity often associated with Tinia; Thufltha, whose exact function remains debated; Nethuns, the Etruscan counterpart of Neptune/Poseidon; and Uni, a major goddess comparable with Juno/Hera.

water.name: Water
water.description: The second four houses include Tecum, a still-mysterious figure connected with dedications around Lake Trasimeno; Lusal, whose reading and identity are disputed; Nethuns, the Etruscan Neptune/Poseidon; and Catha, an astral deity whose solar or lunar character is debated.

earth.name: Earth
earth.description: The terrestrial realm of vegetation, boundaries, and earth spirits. Governs agricultural cycles, forest boundaries, and land-based divine forces.

underworld.name: Underworld
underworld.description: The chthonic realm of earth goddesses, protective spirits, and underworld deities. Controls death omens, protection, and liminal passages.

pars_familiaris.name: Pars Familiaris
pars_familiaris.description: The familiar/favorable realm containing household spirits and benevolent deities. Represents favorable omens and domestic divine protection.

gall_bladder.name: Gall Bladder
gall_bladder.description: The bile reservoir is a charged divinatory area containing Tvnth, Maris, Laran, Letham, and Nethuns. Several identifications in this zone remain debated.

central_section.name: Central Section
central_section.description: The central zone contains Hercle, Maris, Letham, Metlvmth, and Tluscva. It combines better documented divine names with obscure forms whose status remains uncertain.

pars_hostilis.name: Pars Hostilis
pars_hostilis.description: The hostile/unfavorable realm containing border guardians and infernal deities. Represents challenging omens and protective boundaries.

back.name: Back
back.description: The foundational cosmic anchors representing the Sun and Moon. These mark the fundamental celestial cycles underlying all divination.

tinia.description: Supreme sky god and father of the gods in the Etruscan pantheon.

cilens.description: Deity attested on the liver and often associated with Tinia; nocturnal or boundary interpretations remain tentative.

thufltha.description: Female deity attested on the liver and in votive contexts; links with fate, Fortuna, or Tyche are debated rather than secure.

nethuns.description: Water and sea god, securely comparable with Neptune/Poseidon; atmospheric readings belong to specific liver interpretations.

uni.description: Major goddess comparable with Juno/Hera, associated with cities, birth, sovereignty, and in some evidence warlike or astral aspects.

mae.description: Unresolved paired name or epithet in the Uni/Mae inscription; function and equivalent remain uncertain.

tecvm.description: Obscure deity known from the liver and dedications around Lake Trasimeno; function remains debated.

lusal.description: Disputed reading or deity label; some scholarship relates lvsl/lvsal forms to Usil, while this site keeps Lusal as a navigation label.

catha.description: Astral deity, probably female; solar, lunar, underworld, and childbirth associations are debated in current scholarship.

fufluns.description: God of wine, inebriation, and vegetation cycles.

selvans.description: God of forests, pastures, and liminal lands or boundaries.

tluscva.description: Obscure, probably female chthonic divinity or divine collective; interpretation remains disputed.

cels.description: Cel/Cels, earth goddess connected with chthonic forces.

culsans.description: Benevolent protector of doors and thresholds.

alpans.description: Alpan/Alpans, female attendant spirit, perhaps a Lasa, associated with Turan and harmony.

vetis.description: Obscure chthonic deity, sometimes compared with Veiovis; the identification remains conjectural.

pul.description: Unresolved deity name or inscriptional form; function remains uncertain.

lasl.description: Lasa/Lasl, female divine attendant often linked with Turan; fate or service roles are possible.

maris.description: Important but obscure deity, often represented as child or youth in Etruscan evidence; generative interpretations remain debated.

laran.description: God of war, comparable with Mars and Ares.

tvnth.description: Uncertain deity in the gall bladder zone.

hercle.description: Major Etruscan god equivalent to Herakles/Hercules, with protective and oracular associations.

metlvmth.description: Unresolved inscriptional form, possibly an epithet or attribute rather than a secure independent deity.

letham.description: Obscure deity attested on the liver; gender and sphere are debated, with chthonic and birth-related interpretations both proposed.

velch.description: Obscure deity or divine form, possibly related to Volcanus/Vulcan and fire or metalworking traditions.

satres.description: Obscure deity on the liver; any relationship with Saturn remains debated and should be treated as tentative.

usil.description: The sun god, representing solar power and illumination.

tiur.description: Tiur/Tivr, moon deity or moon/month term; on the liver it marks the lunar side of the back.
